chapter: The Raeburn band: people and touring
title: Oscar Pettiford, the Commodore, and Roy Eldridge sitting in
summary: They recall Pettiford and the hotel, and Roy Eldridge sat in after hearing the radio.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And Oscar Pettiford was on the band for a while?
For a while. He was with us--one of the New York Hotels he was there for a while.
Commodore, wasn't it?
Right. We were at the Commodore. The Commordore is the one on 42nd Street; isn't it?
Yeah, Grand Central Station.
Right; that's the one. Where was the Lincoln?
The Lincoln was in Washington.
No, no, the New York
hotel.
What the hell was the Washington hotel that you were at?
I'm not sure whether the Lincoln Hotel is in New York now.
I'm trying to remember where the hell it was.
I think it might be one of those Sixth Avenue hotels.
I can't place it.

When you were at the Lincoln, Jack tells the story that Roy Eldridge came home from a gig or a recording session and went to bed with the radio on and heard an air shot from the Lincoln Hotel, got dressed and came down and asked to sit in and worked with the band for the rest of the time there.
It's possible, I don't remember it, but I remember Roy being there too. Right, Roy was there for a few weeks. Boy, you're bringing back memories, Bill. Right, Roy Eldridge was there.
That's the guy who, when I was a child, go ask to sit in on other children's bands.
How did Roy Eldridge come up to this band and ask to sit in?
A lot of guts. Imagine having been undressed and in bed listening to the radio and being stern enough to get up, get dressed. It sounds like something he would do anyway.

I don't know how to state this. You people in those days were all inventing a new business, you were all like the fresh guys in the Pony Express or whatever. There was a certain amount of we're all in this together. Things would happen then that nobody would think of doing now.
That's exactly true; that's a perfect description. We were all involved with the thing because we knew something was happening, and this was even before the new
writing set in.
Oh, yeah, the idea of the swing band, so to speak, was such a new concept.
